title: Isolation, Cryopreservation and Thawing of Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells
author: CAN-ASC Canadian Autoimmunity Standardization Core
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.brrsm56e

steps.title: Draw blood with anticoagulant
steps.instruction: Draw blood into the appropriate anticoagulant tube, fill to the top, immediately invert 5 times to prevent clotting, and note the draw time; use citric acid, serum, heparin, then EDTA if multiple tube types are needed, and record the order of collection.

steps.title: Collect and freeze plasma (optional)
steps.instruction: If plasma is required, centrifuge the blood 5 min at 500 × g, collect the clear plasma into new tubes and chill on ice; then centrifuge the plasma at 4 °C for 10 min at maximum speed, collect the supernatant and freeze at –80 °C in screw‑top tubes with O‑rings for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Dilute blood with PBS
steps.instruction: Invert the blood to mix, transfer from collection tubes to Falcon tubes, note the original blood volume and add an equal volume of PBS (first rinse the collection tubes). If plasma was collected, add extra PBS so the final volume equals 2 × the original blood volume. Keep the blood at room temperature (avoid chilling), use insulated boxes for shipping, and process within 3 h (avoid delays >24 h). For buffy‑coat starting material, increase the original volume by 3–4 × with PBS.

steps.title: Add density gradient medium
steps.instruction: Add density‑gradient medium (e.g., Ficoll or Lymphoprep) to each Falcon tube at 0.43 mL per 1 mL of blood (e.g., 15 mL medium for 35 mL blood).

steps.title: Layer diluted blood onto gradient
steps.instruction: Slowly overlay the diluted blood onto the surface of the gradient medium without turbulence: tilt the tube horizontally, let the blood run down the side and pool over the gradient, building the layer gradually; avoid mixing and keep the interface crisp.

steps.title: Centrifuge gradient and harvest PBMCs
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 580 × g (1700 rpm) for 30 min at room temperature with acceleration set to 1 and brake set to 0; immediately remove the tube without disturbing the layers.

steps.title: Collect PBMC interface
steps.instruction: Using a sterile transfer pipette, collect the cloudy PBMC layer at the Ficoll‑plasma interface, transfer to a 50 mL Falcon tube containing ~25 mL washing buffer (2 % FBS in PBS), taking as little density medium as possible, then top up to 50 mL with washing buffer. Do not combine more than two PBMC layers in one wash tube.

steps.title: First wash of PBMCs
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 450 × g (1500 rpm) for 10 min at room temperature and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Low‑speed platelet wash
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in washing buffer, centrifuge at 130 × g (800 rpm) for 10 min, then carefully aspirate the supernatant with a large pipette, leaving ~1 mL of washing buffer covering the loose PBMC pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend to original volume and count
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in washing buffer to a volume approximately equal to the original blood volume, take an aliquot for counting, and distinguish RBCs from lymphocytes by lysing RBCs beforehand or using a nuclear stain.

steps.title: Final wash before cryopreservation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the suspension at 450 × g (1500 rpm) for 5 min at room temperature, then prepare cryopreservation tubes.

steps.title: Resuspend cells in CryoStor CS‑10
steps.instruction: Remove all supernatant and resuspend the cells in 1 × CryoStor CS‑10 (or an equivalent lab‑made cryoprotectant) at room temperature to a concentration of 2 × 10⁶–50 × 10⁶ cells/mL; note the strong exothermic reaction when DMSO mixes with aqueous solutions.

steps.title: Aliquot and controlled‑rate freeze
steps.instruction: Aliquot the cell suspension into 2 mL cryovials (minimum volume 250 µL). Freeze using a CoolCell, Mr Frosty (at room temperature), or a controlled‑rate freezer. Place the devices in a –80 °C freezer for at least 16 h (overnight), then transfer vials to liquid‑nitrogen vapor phase on dry ice. For volumes <250 µL use short cryotubes of the same diameter. Cool at 1 °C/min. Replace isopropanol in Mr Frosty after every fifth use and ensure the CoolCell core ring is inserted.

steps.title: Store cryovials in liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Store the frozen vials in liquid‑nitrogen vapor phase (preferred) and, if shipping, use a liquid‑nitrogen dewar; keep the temperature as stable as possible.

steps.title: Prepare thawing solution
steps.instruction: Pre‑heat 10 mL of thawing solution to 37 °C (avoid chilled medium). Thawing medium is RPMI supplemented with 10 % FBS; for granulocyte‑contaminated samples add DNAse (10–20 U/mL) or Benzonase (25–50 U/mL). Alternatives such as BSA or HSA may be used after testing.

steps.title: Rapid thaw cryovials
steps.instruction: Rapidly thaw each cryovial by partial immersion in a 37 °C water bath for 5 min, then transfer the contents into the pre‑warmed thawing solution, handling gently to avoid bubbles. Rinse the cryovial with some of the diluted cell suspension. Wear appropriate PPE, especially for vials stored in liquid‑phase nitrogen.

steps.title: Post‑thaw centrifugation and wash
steps.instruction: Immediately centrifuge the thawed cells for 5 min at 500 × g at room temperature, discard the supernatant, then gently flick the pellet and resuspend in 10 mL of room‑temperature assay buffer. Centrifuge again under the same conditions and discard the supernatant. If downstream assays are serum‑free, repeat the wash to ensure complete removal of serum and DMSO.

steps.title: Final resuspension and viability assessment
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final pellet in assay buffer, take an aliquot for counting, and adjust to the desired assay concentration. Assess viability with an apoptosis assay (e.g., Annexin V with a live‑cell dye) rather than trypan blue alone; optionally rest cells overnight at 37 °C at 2–5 × 10⁶ cells/mL before use.
